item.title: Tatyana Ali’s James Avery Tribute Ends In Tears With Alfonso Ribeiro
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Tatyana Ali and Alfonso Ribeiro reunited on "Dancing With The Stars" to honor James Avery with a personal musical tribute.
item.content:encoded:
Tatyana Ali reunited with Alfonso Ribeiro on “Dancing With The Stars” to honor James Avery, bringing two members of the “Fresh Prince Of Bel-Air” family onto the same dance floor.

The October 20 performance honored the man who played their father, Philip “Uncle Phil” Banks. Ali took part in the show’s Dedication Night with her professional partner, Jan Ravnik, before Ribeiro joined her for the closing stretch.

Ribeiro now co-hosts the competition. For this dance, he stepped out of that role to share the floor with the actress who played his little sister, Ashley Banks, while he played Carlton.

The performance ended with a tearful hug and a portrait of Avery behind them. Ali also supplied the music in a personal way, recording a cover of Nancy Wilson’s “(You Don’t Know) How Glad I Am” for the Viennese waltz. She said Wilson was one of Avery’s favorite artists.

Wilson’s recording of “(You Don’t Know) How Glad I Am” was a breakthrough for the singer in 1964. It earned her first Grammy, for Best Rhythm & Blues Recording, at the 1965 ceremony.

The tribute reached beyond the characters they played.

“He was very much a father figure for all of us,” Ali said in the episode’s introduction, as quoted by Parade.

Ali said Avery had taught her to see performing as more than a job: it was a way to give something to other people. She had settled on honoring him before she knew whether she would make it to Dedication Night.

Ribeiro said he felt blessed to join her for the tribute. Ali, meanwhile, said she felt lucky they could have that experience together again and believed Avery would have been proud.

Avery died in 2013. His absence has remained part of the cast’s reunions since then. When Ali, Ribeiro and their former castmates gathered in 2017, both actors publicly remembered him alongside their photos from the get-together.

Ali and Ravnik’s routine received 32 points from the four judges, her highest total of the season.

Ali and Ravnik stayed in the competition, as did every other couple. The show announced two eliminations for its next episode.

item.title: Doja Cat Gives Fan A Warning Over Full-Body Concert Prep
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Doja Cat urged a fan to be careful after they shared their full-body grooming plans and asked her to notice them that night.
item.content:encoded:
Doja Cat answered a fan’s full-body grooming pledge with one clear instruction: be careful.

The rapper weighed in on X after a fan said they planned to use Nair and shave their whole body for her. The account added that Ariana was the only other person who had inspired that level of preparation, then asked Doja to notice them that night.

Doja did notice. She quoted the post and wrote, “PLEASE BE CAREFUL WHEN USING NAIR,” followed by a heart emoji and “thank you!!!!”

The fan quickly replied that they were excited to see her and offered reassurance: “i was careful, trust !!”

Nair’s safety guidance carries its own warning: “Irritation or allergic reaction may occur with some people, even if they’ve used it before without adverse effects in the past.” The company calls for a fresh patch test before each use, followed by a 24-hour wait. The company also says each product should be used only on the body areas its packaging specifies.

Doja had addressed fans and appearance in a November 2022 Dazed cover interview. She said she liked taking a conventional idea of beauty and changing it, with personal happiness as her measure.

“I want my fans to learn they don’t have to be like anyone else and the thing they want is already there.”

Her own decision to shave her head had brought pushback from friends and family. She had grown tired of the stress of constantly changing wigs and hairstyles, according to Dazed. But she told the magazine she had never felt more beautiful, and said she felt better wearing less makeup.

That conversation also covered the risks of responding to people online. Doja said she sometimes reacted quickly, enjoyed snapping back and then regretted it when the reaction grew much larger. She described trying looks for fun, even as others interpreted those choices as signs that something was wrong.

The exchange happened Tuesday, the same day Doja’s “Tour Ma Vie World Tour” had a scheduled stop at Sacramento’s Golden 1 Center.

Doja’s next scheduled tour date is October 22 at the Kia Forum in Inglewood, California.

item.title: Kevin Gates Claims He Was Never Legally Married To Dreka, But Judge Still Orders $1M Payout
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Kevin Gates says his marriage to Dreka Gates was never legally official in the first place. Wait a second. The Baton Rouge rapper has maintained that his longtime relationship with Dreka never resulted in a legally recognized marriage. He says they had an Islamic religious ceremony, but Kevin has argued that the necessary legal paperwork was never …
item.content:encoded:
Kevin Gates says his marriage to Dreka Gates was never legally official in the first place. Wait a second.

The Baton Rouge rapper has maintained that his longtime relationship with Dreka never resulted in a legally recognized marriage. He says they had an Islamic religious ceremony, but Kevin has argued that the necessary legal paperwork was never completed. Hmmmm….

Think about that for a second, friend. After years of presenting themselves as husband and wife, the legality of their union is being questioned by K.G.

God acknowledges their one-time love, but not the law?

Dreka filed for divorce in July 2025, citing irreconcilable differences after approximately a decade of marriage. She requested $73,467 per month in financial support, including $46,274 in spousal support and $27,193 in child support. I had not one clue that Kevin Gates was caked up like that.

Still, can someone obtain spousal support from a marriage that one party insists never legally existed?

TMZ reported that a judge ordered proceeds from Kevin’s music catalog to be directed toward substantial payments benefiting Dreka. This is to the tune of $929,341.50 – for child and spousal support. There’ $150,000 going directly to her.

There attorney fees, accounting costs and mediation.

The couple shares two children, Islah and Khaza, and child support obligations generally exist regardless of the parents’ marital status. Man, Kevin and Dreka were once considered one of Hip-Hop’s more enduring partnerships. She was more than his romantic companion – she was a significant role in his career and business operations.

Now, the relationship that helped build a musical enterprise has become a battle over the proceeds.

Was this a legally recognized marriage or merely a religious union that never received official documentation? And does it matter?

I am certain the courts will have the final say. Also, I want to know about common law marriages…because 10 years.

item.title: Kash’s Mother Alleges Death Threats
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kash's family mourned the 29-year-old reality star after the Oakland shooting that led to charges against her sister.
item.content:encoded:
Kash‘s mother told TMZ her daughter received death threats, without linking them to her killing.

The reality star, whose real name was Mackayla Paige, died after an October 11 confrontation in downtown Oakland. She was 29.

Oakland police said her sister, Vernika Dunbar, tried to strike another woman with a gun during a fight involving Kash. The weapon fired and hit Kash, according to the police account described by ABC7.

Dunbar was charged with involuntary manslaughter, assault with a firearm and carrying a loaded firearm in public.

An October 14 report by The San Francisco Standard gave more detail on what Dunbar told police. She said the gun had gone off by mistake. Oakland police said Dunbar’s statement fit the surveillance video of the fight, according to the arrest report cited by the publication.

Before the gunfire, the sisters were with two other women on 14th Street, the report said. Kash then got into a fight with another woman. Dunbar got the gun from one of the two women in their group, police alleged. The arrest report described Dunbar as trying to help her sister.

Alongside the felony counts, the Standard reported a misdemeanor charge of brandishing a firearm in public. Officers found Kash wounded around 1:30 A.M. before she was taken to a hospital, where she died, according to the department’s account.

The family had already raised concerns about the attention Kash received outside her television work. Her father, Mack Paige Jr., previously described public threats while asking people to stop directing hate toward Dunbar.

He also said Kash had wanted a break from reality TV and hoped to work as a makeup artist. Her cousin, Azima King, described similar hopes in an ABC7 interview after the shooting.

“She just wanted better for her life. And she wanted to be better. And she wanted to change,” King said.

ABC7’s October 15 coverage described a memorial growing in Oakland. King spoke to the station the day after Kash died and said she was still shaking. The network behind Kash’s reality shows, Now That’s TV, also posted a tribute on October 11.

item.title: Eminem’s Ex-Employee Pleads Guilty Over Stolen Music
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Joseph Strange pleaded guilty in Eminem's stolen-music case and faces sentencing in January after selling unreleased recordings.
item.content:encoded:
Eminem‘s former employee Joseph Strange pleaded guilty Thursday to criminal copyright infringement in a case over the rapper’s unreleased music.

The Justice Department said Strange, 48, sold at least 10 files online for about $50,000 in July and August 2024. Eminem had not known about or approved those sales.

Prosecutors said the files had been accessed more than eight million times by November 2025. They estimated the infringement amount at $750,000 or more. Some tracks had been mastered for possible sale, but a release was not certain or about to happen.

“Today’s guilty plea reinforces a simple principle: accountability follows those who compromise the integrity of another person’s creative labor,” FBI Detroit chief Jennifer Runyan said.

Strange had worked at Eminem’s studio in Ferndale, Michigan, from 2007 to 2021. His job included helping run the computer system that stored music still in progress.

He could access files the studio kept private. Investigators accused him of taking music from drives that needed passwords and stayed offline in a locked safe. They said studio logs showed files had left the drives while Strange still worked there, years before they reached the public.

The staff learned of the leak in January 2025, after unfinished Eminem tracks went up for sale online. An image posted there also matched a private list on a studio drive. Staff called the FBI, and several buyers then identified Strange to agents.

The first case also charged him with moving stolen property across state lines. Prosecutors later filed a new one-count copyright charge in August 2026. It accused him of copying and sharing the music for financial gain. The filing did not include a signed plea agreement or proposed sentence. Strange had not yet admitted guilt.

Eminem’s spokesman Dennis Dennehy had called the alleged theft a betrayal of the rapper and others who worked on the music.

“We will continue to take any and all steps necessary to protect Eminem’s art and will stop at nothing to do so,” he previously said.

Strange’s sentencing is set for January 27, 2027. He faces up to five years in prison. A judge will decide his sentence.

item.title: Westside Gunn Makes His Mass Appeal Move With “HEELMATIC”
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Westside Gunn set "HEELMATIC" for November 13 and launched his Mass Appeal rollout with the Denny LaFlare-produced "ZILLA."
item.content:encoded:
Westside Gunn is taking his next album to Mass Appeal.

HEELMATIC is due November 13 through the label and Griselda Records, with 16 tracks on the way.

The October 22 announcement came with the formal release of “ZILLA,” a track produced by longtime collaborator Denny LaFlare. Gunn’s team called it his first release with Mass Appeal.

The song’s video isn’t new. It premiered on Instagram on August 26, according to Gunn’s team. “ZILLA” now leads the label rollout ahead of the full album next month.

Gunn has kept making records since he talked about quitting in 2022.

HEELMATIC” follows last year’s HEELS HAVE EYES trilogy, an EP and two albums.

He explained what kept him going in an Interview magazine conversation published on October 19, 2023:

“Last year I wanted to hang it up. I was telling people I’m going to retire because I was fed up with the game.”

But he didn’t want to leave before fans knew his story. He said he had held back parts of himself to please his underground audience.

As he made music in 2023, he wanted to let fans hear more of who he was before he walked away.

The work with LaFlare also builds on a bond Gunn described years ago. He told The FADER in 2022 that he saw LaFlare and fellow producer Conductor Williams as family. He wanted them to spend time with him and get to know him, not just send beats.

His work wasn’t limited to his own records. He also shaped projects for rappers Armani Caesar and Rome Streetz:

“I pick the beats. I name the songs. I put them in order. I put the skits on it. I do the cover.”

For his own music, he said he could have the beats mapped out before he wrote his rhymes. Short bursts of recording, rather than constant trips to the studio, could yield more than one project in a year.

Next comes “Heel The World Tour 2: Still Healing!” across Europe and the United Kingdom in early 2027, starting January 30 in Brussels and running through February.

item.title: Roger Goodell Won’t Confirm Jay-Z Super Bowl Report
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Roger Goodell declined to confirm Jay-Z's reported Super Bowl booking, saying the NFL had not made an announcement.
item.content:encoded:
NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell wouldn’t confirm Jay-Z‘s reported Super Bowl halftime booking when he faced questions about the possible performance at an October 21 news conference.

Speaking at a New York news conference after league owners met, Goodell said he was unaware of a leak and had been in the committee meetings, Front Office Sports reported.

“So I’m not sure it’s a leak. We haven’t announced anything. Until we do, we won’t make any comment on that.”

Goodell was addressing a Puck report that Jay-Z would perform. His answer did not rule out the rapper, but it did not turn that report into an official booking, either.

Jay-Z had left the door open at the January 2024 red-carpet premiere of “The Book of Clarence.” He told Entertainment Tonight that choosing himself too early would have been selfish. “Maybe one year,” he said.

Jay-Z’s Roc Nation organizes the halftime show through its partnership with the league. That role involves more people than the artist whose name is now being discussed for the stage.

In 2024, Seth Dudowsky was the NFL’s head of music and its point person for NFL musical events. He also worked as the league’s liaison with Jay-Z’s Roc Nation. He told the Associated Press the goal was to let artists express themselves while keeping the show relevant to both the culture of its host city and what was happening more broadly.

Snoop Dogg, who performed in 2022, credited Jay-Z and NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell for helping open the halftime stage to Hip-Hop. “Shout out to Jay-Z for changing the climate. Roger Goodell for giving him an opportunity,” he told AP.

An unnamed source told the Daily Mail in September that Jay-Z could perform with guests if organizers could not secure a single superstar, as AllHipHop reported.

That earlier account described a possible fallback plan, not an accepted booking.

Super Bowl LXI is scheduled for February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

item.title: Digga D Gets Three Months To Pay $268K In Drug Profits Or Face Prison
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Digga D was ordered to repay £201,039 within three months or face two years in prison, while his lawyer said he could pay.
item.content:encoded:
Digga D was given three months to repay $268,000, with two years in prison at stake if he failed to pay.

Judge Simon Hirst imposed the confiscation order at Lincoln Crown Court on October 21, the BBC reported.

The rapper, whose legal name is Rhys Herbert, had already been released from prison.

Judge Hirst had sentenced him to three years and 11 months on January 31, 2025. Digga D had pleaded guilty to drug import and supply charges.

The two sides had disagreed over how much he had sold and whether he did so for profit.

Digga D argued that much of the cannabis was for him and his circle, with only a small amount sold.

In those sentencing remarks, Judge Hirst rejected that account. He found that Digga D had sold at least 45 kilograms of cannabis for commercial profit. The judge also found that he had supplied the drug over at least seven months, from January through July 2023.

The financial order focused on the proceeds of the offenses. In its guidance, the Crown Prosecution Service explained that confiscation aimed to take away the financial benefit a defendant obtained through crime.

The amount a court seeks to recover can also depend on what the defendant can pay.

That calculation is not always the same as the total benefit figure. Courts generally start with the value of the criminal benefit, but a defendant can show that the assets available to meet the order are worth less. In that situation, the recoverable sum can be the smaller amount.

Nonpayment carries a separate enforcement process. The CPS guidance said authorities could ask the magistrates’ court to activate the prison term set in case of default. Serving that time would not wipe out the debt, so prison would not replace the obligation to pay the money.

The guidance also explained that unpaid confiscation sums can accrue interest after the payment deadline. Paying the full sum by the deadline avoids that interest and the risk of serving the default term.

At the October 21 hearing, defense lawyer Ryan Thompson told the court Digga D had the funds to pay, the BBC reported.

item.title: Chrisean Rock And Blueface’s Family Reunion Takes The Craziest Twist Ever
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Blueface and Chrisean Rock's latest reconciliation appears to be unraveling after a frightening gun confrontation with the cops.
item.content:encoded:
Blueface may have finally reached his breaking point with Chrisean Rock. The pair had a frightening, terrifying confrontation involving armed cops. Their young son and a disagreement that has spilled into public view.

And just like that, the reconciliation that had everybody talking could be headed straight for the dumpster.

And just when we thought these two had finally found some peace! What happened?

The Cuh-RIP rapper and his equally wild partner are at odds following an October 19 incident in Santa Clarita, California, that resulted in Blueface being arrested. The whole ordeal began when authorities responded to a report of someone allegedly pointing a firearm at another person near a Yard House restaurant. This was another swatting situation that he’s been dealing with for a minute now.

Deputies arrived with guns drawn, only to discover there was apparently no armed suspect. A swatting hoax, y’all.

Blueface, per usual, still ended up in handcuffs.

Then his doting fiancee comes in the mix.

Chrisean Rock was there with their three-year-old son when the mess unfolded. And according to the couple’s subsequent statements, they have drastically different views of what happened.

Blueface was furious about Chrisean’s decision to retrieve their child from a vehicle while officers had their weapons drawn.

“I’m not a female I would never do that. I would never see a female in the middle of a motherf##king standoff and pick up my child.”

He took it to the next level in the rant.

“Man, killed this b#tch,” he said to the non-present police. “My son in the car…k#ll this b#tch. This b#tch 26 years old…k#ll this b#tch. My son is three years old. F#ck this b#tch. What the f#ck? You (women) really stand behind b#tches like “Yeah she’s loyal.” No, the b#tch is stupid. The b#tch is dumb.”

Wow. He emptied the clip. No pun intended.

Chrisean, however, insists she was protecting her family.

“They got the gun and put it towards Blue, b#tch! I went and got the baby from the car seat and walked out front of the front of the f#cking gun ni##a,” she yelled in a video.

She apparently believed standing beside Blueface during the terrifying encounter demonstrated loyalty.

“I’m sticking with you like a family, they had a gun in your face.”

Well, there you have it.

One person believes loyalty means standing together regardless of the circumstances. The other believes protecting their child should supersede everything, including romantic devotion.

Now, remember that these two recently appeared to be enjoying a romantic resurgence – engaged! We saw the proposal! The private jet photographs! And those happy family moments suggested their tumultuous history was over.

Not! Blueface – give it another shot! Get some therapy!

The saddest part is that their little boy was caught in the middle of an already dangerous situation.

Are Blueface and Chrisean Rock finally finished?

Or will another reconciliation follow once the emotions subside?

Let’s make peace over proving a point the big picture.

Maybe, we’ll get this again.

item.title: AKA Trial Witness Reports Threats As Others Ask To Stay Off TV
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: AKA trial witnesses asked to keep their faces off TV after the state said one witness received threats following his testimony.
item.content:encoded:
AKA‘s murder trial took a tense turn when the state said a witness had received threats after his face appeared in the news.

Prosecutor Elvis Gcweka raised the claim in the Durban High Court on October 20. He said the man told him about the threats after he took the stand the day before, EWN reported.

The news left other witnesses worried about being shown on TV. They still wanted to come to court and speak, Gcweka said. They asked to keep their faces off the screen because of fears for their safety or their work.

“Their only request is that their faces must not be shown on TV,” Gcweka said, The Citizen reported.

Judge Nomfundo Sipunzi then ruled that the next witness’s face must stay off TV. The order covered that witness, not every person yet to take the stand.

The reports did not name a sender or link the threats to any of the seven men on trial. The claim came from the state, not a court finding that one of the accused had threatened a witness.

The court had just heard about footage of AKA at the airport on the day he died. A man could be seen moving behind him, and the defense questioned who could be named from those images. The witness did not identify the man in the footage as one of the accused.

All seven men pleaded not guilty. The state must prove its case against each man, and the trial has not reached a verdict.

The new plea also came after a fight over what the public could see and hear from court. At first, Judge Sipunzi barred news reports on what witnesses said on the stand. She changed the rule on October 7, allowing the press to report their accounts and the exhibits shown in court.

But that change did not open the door to naming witnesses. Their names and personal details remained off limits under the court’s rule.

Last week, two witnesses spoke from another courtroom. They feared being named or facing the accused as they told the court about men they saw near the scene after the shots.

AKA and Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane were shot dead outside Wish restaurant in Durban on February 10, 2023.
